summary: Targeted correction set for Unity Geography Paper 2 (20 lessons) after the site owner's rulings. Liverpool ONE's car park set to the verified 3,000 spaces in lesson 7 (body, key fact, knowledge check and flashcard), so lessons 7 and 8 now agree. The Maldives literacy example in lesson 9 replaced with Equatorial Guinea, whose high GDP per person sits against a life expectancy of about 64 years. Lesson 14 now labels the 140,000 Goa figure as international arrivals and separates it from the jobs total; no total visitor figure could be verified on Wikipedia or the Goa tourism department site, so none was added. Lesson 16's 'recycling 100 million tonnes of waste' replaced with 'about 100,000 tonnes of waste-derived fuel a year' after no published Hanson or Heidelberg Materials figure for Ribblesdale could be found. All 20 descriptions were over 100 characters and were shortened.

1_liverpool_one_parking.verified: 3,000 spaces - Wikipedia, Liverpool ONE: 'The park conceals a 3,000-space underground car park'; infobox Parking: 3,000
1_liverpool_one_parking.applied: L7 content_html x2, L7 knowledge_checks[2].options[2], L7 flashcard_questions[12].a; L8 already said 3,000 so it is unchanged

2_maldives_literacy.verified: Equatorial Guinea GDP per capita about $20,017 PPP (Wikipedia, Equatorial Guinea); life expectancy 63.7 years, 2022 estimate (Wikipedia, Demographics of Equatorial Guinea); world average 73.17 years
2_maldives_literacy.applied: L9 content_html key fact; the Maldives appears nowhere else in the lesson

3_goa_tourists.verified: no total visitor figure found - Wikipedia (Goa, Tourism in Goa, Tourism in India) and goatourism.gov.in give no annual total; the India tourism statistics portal returned 403
3_goa_tourists.applied: L14 content_html; 140,000 relabelled as international arrivals and the 250,000-300,000 jobs attributed to tourism as a whole. No total added because none could be verified.
3_goa_tourists.note: The practice question in L14 repeats the jobs figure without the 140,000, so it needed no change.

4_castle_cement_waste.verified: unverifiable - Wikipedia has no Ribblesdale Cement article and the Castle Cement article gives no fuel data; heidelbergmaterials.co.uk works pages returned 404
4_castle_cement_waste.applied: L16 content_html key fact set to 'burning about 100,000 tonnes of waste-derived fuel a year instead of coal'; L16 conclusion_html takeaway aligned
